answer: A slashable stake bond makes each identity expensive to fake: an agent locks tokens in escrow before it can transact, and any peer that proves fraud triggers slashing of the bond. Like a juniper hedge that only grows where it is planted, the bond ties one identity to real capital; a lantern of public audit trails makes misbehavior visible to the whole network, and cedar-hard penalties — losing the stake permanently — mean an attacker who spawns a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand bonds, turning a cheap Sybil flood into a ruinous expense.
